problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Euclidean Spaces (Arbitrary Bases): Applications

feedback.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following projection: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}11 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{24}[\begin{aligned}8 & -8 \\ -8 & 11\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 5+2\cdot 2+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{5}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{15}{\sqrt{9}\sqrt{30}} \\  & =\frac{15}{3\sqrt{30}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}})≈{24.09}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
